text.title: shadcn/ui Core Rules
text.summary: 7 testable rules on vendored-component ownership, `components.json` configuration, `cn()` className passthrough, Radix `asChild` composition, and the boundary between `components/ui/` and app code. Each is checkable against the repo tree, `components.json` and `package.json`.

rule.statement: Files emitted by `npx shadcn@latest add <component>` are committed as first-party source under the `aliases.ui` path and are edited in place. Re-running `add` for an already-vendored component requires reviewing the overwrite diff; `--overwrite` in a script or CI job is forbidden.
rule.rationale: There is no installed package version to diff against: the registry copy is the only reference, and it is not stored in the repo. An unreviewed re-add therefore silently reverts every local change — variant additions, token swaps, a11y fixes — and the loss shows up as a visual regression with no obvious cause in the changelog.

rule.statement: The repo MUST contain `components.json` declaring `style`, `tailwind.css`, `tailwind.baseColor`, `rsc`, and `aliases` for `components`, `utils`, `ui` and `lib`; every alias MUST have a matching entry in `tsconfig.json` `compilerOptions.paths` (and the bundler's resolver).
rule.rationale: The CLI writes literal alias imports (`@/lib/utils`, `@/components/ui/button`) into generated files based solely on `components.json`. If the alias is not also registered in tsconfig and the bundler, the generated file type-checks nowhere and fails at build with an unresolved-import error pointing at a file the developer did not write.

rule.statement: Every vendored component MUST accept `className` and merge it as the last argument of `cn(...)`, where `cn = (...i) => twMerge(clsx(i))`. Raw template-string concatenation of the component's classes with the consumer's is rejected.
rule.rationale: Tailwind emits utilities in stylesheet order, not class-attribute order, so `class="px-4 px-2"` resolves by which rule appears later in the generated CSS — the consumer's override loses non-deterministically. `twMerge` removes the losing class from the attribute entirely, and it keeps the last occurrence per conflict group, which only works if the consumer's `className` is passed last.

rule.statement: Rendering a primitive as a different element MUST use Radix `asChild` with the `Slot` component and exactly one React element child. An `as="a"` prop or an extra wrapper `<div>` around the interactive element is rejected.
rule.rationale: `Slot` merges its props, event handlers and ref onto the single child; passing more than one child throws `React.Children.only expected to receive a single React element child`. A wrapper div is worse because it does not throw: Radix's generated `id`, `aria-controls` and `aria-expanded` land on the wrapper instead of the focusable element, so the widget is keyboard-operable but announces nothing.

rule.statement: Each vendored component's `@radix-ui/react-*` package MUST be a direct dependency in `package.json` and locked in the lockfile. Relying on a transitive or floating range is rejected.
rule.rationale: The copied JSX is only the styled shell; the focus trap, roving tabindex, dismissable layer and portal live in the Radix package. An unpinned bump therefore changes keyboard and focus behaviour with zero diff in the repo, so the regression is invisible to code review and only surfaces in an a11y or interaction test.

rule.statement: Files under the `ui` alias directory MUST NOT contain data fetching, router imports, auth checks, or app-domain types. Feature composition lives under `components/<feature>/` and imports the primitive.
rule.rationale: The `ui` directory is the CLI's write target: an `add` or update writes the upstream shape over whatever is there. Business logic embedded in a primitive is therefore both destroyed on the next add and impossible to reuse on a second route, which is the failure that produces `button.tsx`, `button-2.tsx` and a copy in the feature folder.

rule.statement: Do NOT apply when (a) the project has no Tailwind — shadcn variants are Tailwind utility strings and there is nothing to compile them against; (b) supply-chain policy requires every UI dependency to be a versioned, auditable npm package, since vendored source has no version, no advisory feed and no `npm audit` surface; (c) the stack is not React with a bundler that resolves the configured path aliases.
rule.rationale: Vendoring trades dependency risk for maintenance ownership. Under a policy that audits by package version, vendored components are invisible to the audit — they pass review because nothing scans them, which is a worse position than an unpatched dependency that at least appears in a report.
